Initiated under the directives of Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif, the application offers single-platform guidance covering visits to Nankana Sahib, accommodation details, and religious rituals. The tool is designed with offline access and supports seven languages, including English, Urdu, Hindi, and Punjabi, ensuring reliable and timely assistance.

This launch coincides with extensive preparations across Nankana Sahib for the 557th birth anniversary of Baba Guru Nanak, the spiritual founder of Sikhism. All seven local gurdwaras, featuring Gurdwara Janam Asthan, have been adorned with decorative lights and illuminations. Additionally, major city squares, intersections, and the motorway interchange have been brightly lit to welcome pilgrims.

The city is currently showcasing Sikh culture and traditions, with the Punjab government implementing special beautification initiatives to highlight the area's historical and regional significance. These arrangements aim to warmly host international participants attending the birth anniversary celebrations.

In a separate entertainment note mentioned during the events, Indian cricketer Sachin Tendulkar praised actor Ranveer Singh's portrayal of Kapil Dev in the film 83, expressing at the Global Peace Honours 2026 in Mumbai that Singh could easily become a good cricketer.

stories.title: Netanyahu and Eisenkot Coalitions Resume Talks for Israeli Government
stories.summary:
Delegations from the Yashar party, led by former army chief of staff Gadi Eisenkot, and caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud party met at a hotel in Herzliya near Tel Aviv to resume coalition government negotiations. Following October elections that yielded no absolute majority, Eisenkot holds the mandate to form a government until December 6, with a potential 14-day extension. His 48-member bloc requires 61 lawmakers for a majority and remains internally divided on whether to ally with ultra-Orthodox parties, Arab parties, or Likud in a national unity government.

Netanyahu advocates for a national unity government featuring a premiership rotation mechanism. Such a setup could help Netanyahu maintain political shielding against ongoing corruption charges and block an independent commission of inquiry into security failures before the October 7, 2023, Hamas raid. However, Eisenkot and his ally Naftali Bennett have previously rejected serving under a cabinet led by Netanyahu.

While Yashar frames the renewed talks as a genuine effort to build the broadest possible administration, Likud has established strict conditions for participation. Likud demands an end to personal attacks against the outgoing prime minister, the exclusion of Arab parties, and shared positions on rejecting a Palestinian state, maintaining territorial control in Syria, Lebanon, and Gaza, and addressing ultra-Orthodox Jewish conscription.

If negotiations fail, Eisenkot has warned of his readiness to bypass prolonged talks by presenting an emergency national government to parliament. This alternative plan could potentially involve forming a minority government supported by core opposition parties, though right-wing allies like Avigdor Liberman strongly oppose cooperating with Arab lawmakers.

stories.title: لکی مروت میں تھانہ صدر کے قریب ریموٹ کنٹرول دھماکے سے چار اہلکار زخمی
stories.summary:
لکی مروت میں تھانہ صدر کی پولیس موبائل کے قریب ایک ریموٹ کنٹرول دھماکا پیش آیا ہے جس کے نتیجے میں چار پولیس اہلکار معمولی زخمی ہو گئے ہیں۔ پولیس حکام کے مطابق تمام زخمی اہلکاروں کو فوری طور پر اسپتال منتقل کر دیا گیا ہے جہاں انہیں ضروری طبی امداد فراہم کی جا رہی ہے۔

واقعے کے فوراً بعد قانون نافذ کرنے والے اداروں نے پورے علاقے کو گھیرے میں لے لیا اور ایک سرچ آپریشن کا آغاز کر دیا گیا۔ اس حملے کے نتیجے میں قریبی ریلوے ٹریک کو بھی نقصان پہنچا ہے جہاں ایک فٹ گہرا گڑھا پڑ گیا ہے، اور ریلوے حکام کا کہنا ہے کہ متاثرہ ٹریک کی بحالی کا کام مکمل ہونے میں کئی گھنٹے درکار ہوں گے۔

اس دھماکے کے بعد سکیورٹی فورسز اور ریسکیو ادارے الرٹ ہو گئے ہیں اور علاقے میں امن و امان بح رکھنے کے لیے کارروائیاں جاری ہیں۔ واقعے کی نوعیت کو دیکھتے ہوئے قانون نافذ کرنے والے اداروں نے تفتیش شروع کر دی ہے تاکہ حملہ آوروں کا سراغ لگایا جا سکے۔

مقامی انتظامیہ اور پولیس حکام زخمی ہونے والے اہلکاروں کی صحت پر نظر رکھے ہوئے ہیں جبکہ ٹریک کی مرمت کا کام بھی جلد شروع کیے جانے کی توقع ہے۔ علاقے میں اضافی نفری تعینات کر کے سکیورٹی کو مزید سخت کر دیا گیا ہے تا کہ کسی بھی ناخوشگوار واقعے سے دوبارہ بچا جا سکے۔

stories.title: پاکستان اور ترکیہ کے درمیان عدالتی تعاون کے فروغ کیلیے مفاہمتی یادداشت پر دستخط
stories.summary:
پاکستان اور ترکیہ کے درمیان عدالتی تعاون کو مزید فروغ دینے کے لیے دارالحکومت اسلام آباد میں ایک اہم تقریب کے دوران مفاہمتی یادداشت پر باضابطہ دستخط کیے گئے ہیں۔ اس معاہدے کا مقصد دونوں برادر ممالک کی اعلیٰ عدالتوں کے درمیان ادارہ جاتی روابط کو مضبوط بنانا اور عدالتی نظام میں باہمی تعاون کی نئی راہیں کھولنا ہے۔

اس یادداشت پر چیف جسٹس آف پاکستان یحییٰ آفریدی اور ترکیہ کے کورٹ آف کیسیشن کے صدر عمر کیرکیز نے دستخط کیے۔ تقریب کے دوران دونوں ممالک کے قومی ترانے بجائے گئے جبکہ چیف جسٹس پاکستان نے مہمانوں کا خیرمقدم کرتے ہوئے اس عزم کا اظہار کیا کہ قانون کی حکمرانی پر پختہ یقین رکھتے ہیں اور یہ معاہدہ دونوں ملکوں کے نظام عدل کو جدید خطوط پر استوار کرے گا۔

ترکیہ کے کورٹ آف کیسیشن کے صدر عمر کرکیز نے تقریب سے خطاب کرتے ہوئے دونوں ممالک کے دیرینہ اور تاریخی برادرانہ تعلقات کو سراہا۔ انہوں نے اس بات پر زور دیا کہ باہمی اعتماد اور مشترکہ اقدار پر مبنی ان تعلقات کو مزید وسعت دینے کے لیے تجربات کا تبادلہ اور جدید ٹیکنالوجی کا استعمال انتہائی ناگزیر ہے۔

یہ معاہدہ خاص طور پر ضلعی عدلیہ کی تربیت اور مصنوعی ذہانت سمیت جدید ٹیکنالوجی کے فروغ میں معاون ثابت ہوگا۔ اس سے ای کورٹس کے ذریعے انصاف تک رسائی بہتر ہوگی اور دونوں ممالک کے نظام انصاف میں جدت آئے گی جو کہ عدالتی تعاون کو ایک نئی بلندی پر لے جائے گا۔

stories.title: امریکہ کی بندرگاہوں اور کارگو جہازوں کو روزانہ ہزاروں سائبر حملوں کا سامنا
stories.summary:
امریکہ میں بحری شعبے کو شدید سکیورٹی چیلنجز کا سامنا ہے جہاں ملک کی بندرگاہوں اور کارگو جہازوں کو روزانہ کی بنیاد پر ہزاروں سائبر حملوں کی کوششوں کا نشانہ بنایا جا رہا ہے۔ ان حملوں میں ڈیجیٹل سسٹمز، مواصلاتی نیٹ ورکس اور کارگو کی نقل و حرکت پر نظر رکھنے والے کمپیوٹر سسٹمز کو ہدف بنایا جا رہا ہے۔

ٹیکساس میں واقع پورٹ آف کارپس کرسٹی، جو خام تیل برآمد کرنے والی امریکہ کی سب سے بڑی بندرگاہ ہے اور روزانہ تقریباً 23 لاکھ بیرل خام تیل کی برآمدات سنبھالتی ہے، کو روزانہ سینکڑوں اور بعض اوقات ہزاروں سائبر حملوں کا سامنا کرنا پڑتا ہے۔ اسی طرح لاس اینجلس کی بندرگاہ نے بھی رواں سال اگست کے مہینے میں سائبر حملوں کی تقریباً 12 کروڑ کوششیں ناکام بنانے کی اطلاع دی ہے۔

امریکی کوسٹ گارڈ کے جاری کردہ اعداد و شمار کے مطابق گزشتہ برس کے دوران بحری شعبے میں مجموعی طور پر سائبر واقعات میں 17 فیصد تک کا نمایاں اضافہ ریکارڈ کیا گیا ہے۔ ان بڑھتے ہوئے خطرات نے بحری تجارت اور معاشی سرگرمیوں کو خطرات سے دوچار کر دیا ہے۔

ان روزانہ کی بنیاد پر ہونے والے سائبر حملوں کی وجہ سے امریکی حکام انتہائی چوکس ہیں اور بندرگاہوں کے ڈیجیٹل انفراسٹرکچر کو محفوظ بنانے کے لیے ہنگامی اقدامات اٹھائے جا رہے ہیں۔ بحری شعبے میں سائبر سکیورٹی کو بہتر بنانا اب حکام کے لیے ایک اہم ترجیح بن چکا ہے تاکہ تجارتی سرگرمیاں بلا تعطل جاری رہ سکیں۔

stories.title: Oman Challenges Indian Ocean Yellowfin Tuna Catch Quotas
stories.summary:
Oman has officially contested a new fishing quota framework concerning yellowfin tuna in the Indian Ocean, citing potential negative consequences for traditional fishing communities, coastal livelihoods, and the national fisheries sector. The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources filed an objection against Resolution 26/01, which was adopted by the Indian Ocean Tuna Commission (IOTC) during its May 2026 meeting in the Maldives.

A central issue for Oman is the provisional annual catch limit of 25,000 tonnes established by the resolution. Although a five-year transition period is included, Omani authorities argue the cap fails to account for the substantial contributions of artisanal and small-scale operations. Thousands of citizens rely on these fisheries for their income and national food security, prompting Muscat to demand that traditional coastal catches be excluded from total allowable catch calculations.

In tandem with its formal objection, Oman is refining its national fisheries data collection methods, encompassing catch recording, monitoring, sampling, and reporting. These enhancements led to a downward revision of estimated 2025 artisanal and coastal yellowfin tuna catches to approximately 20,000 tonnes. Industrial fishing fleets will continue to face strict supervision and national catch limits.

Oman clarified that its challenge does not permit unrestricted fishing; operators must still adhere to existing requirements under IOTC Resolution 19/01 and national regulations. The nation remains committed to collaborating with the IOTC to foster transparent, sustainable fishing regulations that balance marine conservation with economic needs under Oman Vision 2040.

stories.title: Sindh Rejects Wapda's Ghotki Drainage Project Over Water Safety
stories.summary:
The Sindh irrigation department and the Nara Canal Area Water Board have rejected a proposed Rs156 billion drainage project put forward by the Water and Power Development Authority (Wapda). The Ghotki Drainage Project aims to drain wastewater from Ubauro, Daharki, Khangarh, and Mirpur Mathelo into the Nara Canal, Sindh's largest freshwater perennial canal. Local authorities fear the scheme will contaminate freshwater supplies, degrade soil, and harm drinking water systems for millions of residents.

The project involves a 1,067-kilometer main drain intended to manage agricultural runoff and prevent waterlogging and salinisation in fertile lands. However, Sindh officials heavily criticized the Environmental Impact Assessment, stating it was conducted without consulting local stakeholders, the irrigation department, or the Nara Canal Area Water Board, in violation of the Sindh Water Management Ordinance 2002.

Opposition to the project is deeply rooted in past federal drainage failures, specifically the Left Bank Outfall Drain and Right Bank Outfall Drain networks. Officials noted that past projects caused severe ecological damage, including the destruction of Manchhar Lake and economic ruin for local fishing and farming communities due to design flaws and blocked natural waterways.

Sindh authorities emphasized that the Nara Canal serves as a vital water source for roughly 6.61 million people across multiple districts, the Thar desert, and regional power plants. Because more than half of the proposed catchment area extends outside the Ghotki canal command zone into Punjab, the province firmly maintains that discharging effluent into the Nara Canal is unacceptable.

stories.title: روسی خبر رساں ادارے اسپٹنک نے اردو نیوز سروس کا باقاعدہ آغاز کر دیا
stories.summary:
روس کے معروف خبر رساں ادارے اسپٹنک نے باضابطہ طور پر اپنی اردو نیوز سروس کا آغاز کر دیا ہے، جو پاکستان اور روس کے درمیان میڈیا کے شعبے میں ایک بڑی پیش رفت ہے۔ اسپٹنک اردو زبان میں باقاعدہ نیوز سروس شروع کرنے والا پہلا روسی خبر رساں ادارہ بن گیا ہے، جسے قومی زبان اردو کی عالمی سطح پر بڑھती ہوئی اہمیت کا اعتراف قرار دیا جا رہا ہے۔

وفاقی وزیر اطلاعات و نشریات عطاء اللہ تارڑ نے اس موقع پر اپنے ایک خصوصی ویڈیو پیغام میں ادارے کی انتظامیہ اور پوری ٹیم کو دلی مبارکباد دی۔ انہوں نے کہا کہ یہ اردو سروس پاکستان اور روس کے عوام کو قریب لانے، باہمی اعتماد، عوامی روابط اور فہم و فراست کو فروغ دینے میں انتہائی اہم اور کلیدی کردار ادا کرے گی۔

اس سروس کے آغاز کے موقع پر ماسکو میں روس میں پاکستان کے سفیر فیصل نیاز ترمذی کا پہلا خصوصی انٹرویو بھی ریکارڈ کیا گیا، جو انہوں نے ماسکو اسٹوڈیو میں اردو زبان میں دیا۔ سفیر پاکستان نے اپنے انٹرویو میں پاک روس تعلقات کی اہمیت اور دونوں ممالک کے درمیان میڈیا کے باہمی روابط کو اجاگر کیا۔

واضح رہے کہ اسپٹنک دنیا بھر میں تیس سے زائد زبانوں میں خبریں فراہم کرتا ہے اور اس کے یورپ، ایشیا، افریقہ، لاطینی امریکہ اور مشرق وسطیٰ میں چھبیس ادارتی مراکز قائم ہیں۔ وزیراعظم محمد شہباز شریف کے متوقع دورہ روس سے قبل اس اردو سروس کا آغاز دوطرفہ تعلقات کو مزید مستحکم کرنے میں مددگار ثابت ہوگا۔

stories.title: وزیراعظم شہباز شریف کے دورۂ روس میں اہم معاہدوں کا امکان
stories.summary:
وزیراعظم شہباز شریف کے متوقع دورۂ روس کے دوران پاکستان اور روس کے مابین مختلف شعبوں میں پندرہ سے سولہ معاہدوں پر دستخط کیے جانے کا قوی امکان ہے۔ ان مجوزہ معاہدوں کا بنیادی مقصد دونوں ممالک کے باہمی تعلقات کو فروغ دینا اور دوطرفہ تعاون کو نئی وسعت عطا کرنا ہے۔ یہ دورہ دونوں ملکوں کے درمیان سفارتی اور معاشی تعلقات کے حوالے سے انتہائی اہمیت کا حامل سمجھا جا رہا ہے۔

روس میں پاکستان کے تعینات سفیر فیصل نیاز ترمذی نے مقامی میڈیا سے گفتگو کرتے ہوئے وزیراعظم کے اس دورے کو ایک اہم اور تاریخی قدم قرار دیا ہے۔ ان کا کہنا تھا کہ اس دورے کا مقصد دونوں ریاستوں کے باہمی تعلقات کو مزید مضبوط بنانا ہے۔ سفیر کے مطابق وزیر اعظم شہباز شریف کی ترجیحات میں سیاسی تعلقات کے فروغ کے ساتھ ساتھ تجارت، ثقافت، تعلیم اور عوامی سطح پر رابطوں کو بہتر بنانا بھی شامل ہے۔

 طے شدہ شیڈول کے مطابق وزیراعظم شہباز شریف تیس نومبر سے تین روزہ سرکاری دورے پر روس روانہ ہوں گے۔ اس دورے کے دوران توانائی کے شعبے میں تعاون بڑھانے اور سرمایہ کاری کے معاملات کو آگے بڑھانے پر خصوصی توجہ دی جائے گی تاکہ دونوں ملکوں کے معاشی روابط کو مزید استحکام مل سکے۔

یہ دورہ دونوں ممالک کے درمیان دوطرفہ تجارت، توانائی اور سرمایہ کاری کے شعبوں میں بڑی پیش رفت کا باعث بنے گا اور اس سے باہمی تعاون کے نئے دروازے کھلیں گے۔ ان معاہدوں کے ذریعے مختلف شعبوں میں تعاون کے دائرہ کار کو وسیع کیا جائے گا جس سے دونوں ممالک کے عوام کو براہ راست فائدہ پہنچے گا۔

stories.title: Pakistan Stocks Surge as KSE-100 Gains Nearly 600 Points
stories.summary:
Buying interest lifted the Pakistan Stock Exchange at the start of trading on Monday, pushing the benchmark KSE-100 Index up by nearly 600 points during the opening minutes. At 9:35 am, the index hovered at 177,974.15, marking an increase of 591.58 points or 0.33%. This positive momentum included buying activity across key sectors such as commercial banks, automobile assemblers, fertilizer, power generation, oil and gas exploration companies, and oil marketing companies. Prominent index-heavy stocks like HUBCO, PSO, MARI, OGDC, PPL, POL, HBL, MCB, and MEBL all traded in positive territory.

This rebound follows a marginally lower close the previous week, where domestic political uncertainty regarding a proposed referendum on creating new provinces dampened investor sentiment. That local pressure had counteracted the positive effects of softer international oil prices and lower domestic fuel costs, ultimately causing the KSE-100 Index to drop 491.32 points to settle at 177,382.56 points.

Globally, markets experienced turbulence last week, driven by a sharp sell-off in technology and chip stocks at the core of the artificial intelligence boom. Investors began questioning whether massive, mostly borrowed expenditures on data centers would yield returns quickly enough to satisfy lenders and justify lofty stock valuations. Consequently, the Nasdaq suffered a 10% drop—its largest weekly decline since March 2020—while Taiwan’s benchmark experienced its steepest fall since 1990.

In response to these international declines, authorities worked to stabilize Asian markets, while US stock futures rose on Monday. Early trading saw Nasdaq 100 futures bounce by nearly 3% and S&P 500 futures climb 2%. Meanwhile, Taiwan stocks steadied, and South Korean shares hit a 10-month low before finding support.

stories.title: ڈونلڈ ٹرمپ کا دعویٰ: ایران نے ایک ہفتے میں سب سے زیادہ ڈرونز داغے
stories.summary:
امریکی صدر ڈونلڈ ٹرمپ نے دعویٰ کیا ہے کہ ایران نے صرف گزشتہ ایک ہفتے کے دوران پچھلے ایک سال کے مقابلے میں سب سے زیادہ حملہ آور ڈرونز اور میزائل داغے ہیں۔ انہوں نے اس دعوے کے لیے کسی رپورٹ یا اعداد و شمار کے ماخذ کا ذکر نہیں کیا، تاہم اسے کانگریس کے انتخابات میں ڈেমوکریٹس کی کامیابی اور امریکی شیئر بازاروں کی گراوٹ سے جوڑا۔

دوسری جانب برطانوی میری ٹائم ٹریڈ آپریشنز سینٹر نے بتایا کہ 19 سے 21 نومبر کے دوران امریکی مدد سے 114 جہازوں نے آبنائے ہرمز عبور کی، جو گزشتہ سال کے روزانہ اوسط 138 جہازوں سے کم ہے۔ اسی عرصے میں آبنائے باب المندب سے 68 جہاز گزرے۔ دریں اثنا، امریکی وزارت خارجہ نے بحرین میں موجود امریکی شہریوں کو حوثی حملوں کے خطرات کے پیش نظر زیادہ احتیاط برتنے کی وارننگ دی ہے۔

اسرائیل میں سیاسی صورتحال کے حوالے سے، وزیرِ اعظم بنیامن نیتن یاہو اور یاشار پارٹی کے رہنما گادی آئزنکوٹ کے درمیان اتحادی حکومت کی تشکیل پر ہونے والے مذاکرات کا دوسرا دور بھی بغیر کسی معاہدے کے ختم ہو گیا۔ اکتوبر کے انتخابات میں کسی کو واضح اکثریت نہیں ملی تھی اور سابق فوجی سربراہ گادی آئزنکوٹ کے پاس 6 دسمبر تک حکومت بنانے کا وقت ہے۔

امریکہ میں شمالی کیرولائنا کے انتخابات میں ایک اور ڈیموکریٹ کی کامیابی کے بعد ایوان نمائندگان میں ڈেমوکریٹس کی نشستیں 258 ہو گئی ہیں، جو 1992 کے بعد سب سے بڑی اکثریت ہے۔ صدر ٹرمپ نے اپنے بیان میں کہا کہ ایران کے رہنما ڈیموکریٹس کو کمزور سمجھتے ہیں لیکن وہ ایسا نہیں ہونے دیں گے۔

stories.title: Mian Muhammad Mansha Urges Structural Reforms and Cheaper Energy
stories.summary:
Mian Muhammad Mansha, chairman of Nishat Group and MCB Bank, has emphasized the need for structural reforms, including a smaller government size, lower energy expenses, eliminated bureaucratic hurdles, and upgraded infrastructure to stimulate private investment and employment in Pakistan. Speaking with B&F, he pointed out that excessive overhead, regulatory delays, and an inefficient business climate hinder corporate expansion and job creation.

Drawing parallels to the past privatization of MCB Bank, where 50,000 employees accepted golden handshakes and redirected payouts into new enterprises like schools and restaurants, Mansha argued that public sector downsizing liberates resources for productive economic activities. He also underscored severe infrastructure challenges, particularly at Karachi port, citing high operational costs, inefficient procedures, traffic congestion on route to Punjab, and an unused berth at the former Pakistan Steel Mills left idle for two decades. Furthermore, he noted that transferring terminal operations to foreign private operators doubled port charges without driving new investments.

Bureaucratic bottlenecks remain a significant obstacle, illustrated by a four-month delay his cement company faced simply to secure routine permits for importing free municipal waste from Britain, Denmark, and Italy as alternative fuel. Additionally, soaring electricity tariffs are driving industries away from the national grid toward solar power and battery storage. Mansha warned that declining grid demand could strand costly generation capacity while prompting regulators to restrict solar power instead of fixing underlying sectoral inefficiencies.

To restore industrial competitiveness, Mansha advocated for supporting labor-intensive manufacturing sectors like textiles and garments, reducing the tax burden, and establishing efficient rail freight. He also encouraged expanding regional trade with India, Afghanistan, and Central Asian nations to bolster exports, tourism, and hospitality.

stories.title: Lahore Ranks Well in Safety Index Amid Police Efficiency Reviews
stories.summary:
Lahore achieved favorable standing in Numbeo’s 2026 Mid-Year Crime and Safety Index, scoring ahead of major global cities such as New York, Paris, and New Delhi, though ranking below Islamabad. Presented to Punjab Inspector General of Police Abdul Kareem during his visit to Lahore Police Lines at Qilla Gujjar Singh, the report revealed safety and crime indexes of 63.8 and 36.2, respectively. The high-level meeting included Capital City Police Officer Bilal Siddique Kamyana, DIGs Faisal Kamran and Zeshan Raza, alongside other senior officials.

During the briefing, DIG Kamran noted that Lahore’s crime index placed it in the "Low" to "Moderate" range, outperforming Karachi and Rawalpindi. CCPO Kamyana reported that Lahore is the only city in Punjab free of no-go zones, major land-grabbing mafias, or gangsters, reflecting significant security improvements over the past four years. The discussion also addressed administrative concerns, including SHO posting criteria, missing women cases where fewer than 100 remain untraced, and a shortage of Dolphin Force motorcycles.

IGP Abdul Kareem expressed strong dissatisfaction with the deteriorating emergency response time on helpline 15 calls, which dropped to 22% across the province as callers were frequently told to visit police stations. Although Lahore's response time stood at a higher 66%, the IGP deemed it insufficient given the city's abundant resources. To address the shortage of Dolphin Force bikes, which currently rely on makeshift patrols using various station motorcycles, Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz approved a Rs300 million procurement plan to deliver 300 to 400 new bikes to Lahore Police by December.

The meeting additionally touched upon internal personnel matters, noting complaints from inspectors who felt overlooked for SHO positions in favor of sub-inspectors, a practice the DIG operations defended as a way to cultivate trained personnel for sensitive assignments.

stories.title: US Stock Futures Bounce as Global Markets Recover from AI Rout
stories.summary:
United States stock futures rose on Monday while international officials attempted to stabilize falling markets across Asia following a severe downturn for the technology and semiconductor sectors tied to the artificial intelligence boom. Investors have grown concerned that massive, largely borrowed expenditures on data centres will fail to generate returns quickly enough to satisfy lenders or justify lofty valuations. Last week, the Nasdaq suffered a 10% drop, marking its largest weekly decline since March 2020 during the pandemic panic, while Taiwan experienced its steepest fall since 1990 due to its crucial role as a semiconductor supply chain hub.

During early trading on Monday, Nasdaq 100 futures rebounded by nearly 3% and S&P 500 futures increased by 2%. Markets in Taiwan steadied, whereas South Korean shares dropped about 4% to reach a 10-month low prior to finding support. South Korea's finance minister planned to hold a press conference regarding a potential market stabilization fund to halt further declines. Japanese markets remained closed for a holiday, though futures indicated ongoing selling pressure, and markets in Hong Kong and China retreated to new multi-month lows.

The broader "AI trade," which previously boosted various sectors including cable makers and electricity generators, has faced mounting pressure from rising interest rates. Shares related to artificial intelligence dropped sharply last week following the departure of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and the disappointing market debut of AI firm Anthropic, which closed down 8.5% on its first full day of trading. In response to the volatility, financial regulators in Taiwan ordered stricter short-selling rules on Saturday, and Chinese stock exchanges introduced support measures such as eased margin financing requirements.

Damien Boey, a portfolio strategist at Wilson Asset Management in Sydney, noted that US markets spent three sessions in panic territory last week. Although this can indicate that the worst has passed, Boey cautioned that a lack of central bank policy pivots leaves investors uncertain about whether a durable bounce can materialize without further catalysts. Meanwhile, unrelated entertainment data showed that Netflix's political series The Diplomat remained in the top-five category globally for November.

stories.title: Russian Strikes Kill Six in Kyiv Region Amid Energy Attacks
stories.summary:
Russian aerial bombardments across the Kyiv region on Sunday resulted in at least six deaths, including casualties from a partially collapsed apartment block, as Ukraine faces another winter under ongoing invasion. An overnight strike hit a five-storey building in Dymer, situated about 45 kilometres north of the capital, leaving a mound of smouldering rubble. The State Emergency Service of Ukraine reported recovering three bodies, identifying victims as a woman born in 1978 and a teenager born in 2008. Kyiv region governor Tymur Tkachenko stated that rescuers successfully pulled a child alive from the wreckage on Sunday evening, though emergency crews continued searching for 11 unresponsive people, including two children.

Additional casualties occurred elsewhere in the region during the renewed wave of attacks. In Vyshneve, a strike on a supermarket killed two people and wounded eight others. Another fatality was recorded in Bila Tserkva when a strike ignited a private home. Prime Minister Sergiy Koretsky reported that Russian forces also targeted a power substation in the Dnipropetrovsk region. Moscow has intensified assaults on Ukrainian infrastructure as winter temperatures approach freezing, following a vow by Russian President Vladimir Putin to deliver a painful response to Ukrainian attacks on the Crimean bridge.

The conflict also produced regional spillover in the Baltic Sea and neighbouring countries. Finnish authorities confirmed that the Russian cargo ship Sparta II, which caught fire after a drone attack in international waters in the Gulf of Finland on Saturday, was towed into Russian waters on Sunday. The vessel, which is under US and Ukrainian sanctions for suspected weapons transport from Syria to Russia, drifted into Finnish waters near Helsinki before being secured. Mikko Hirvi of the Finnish Border Guard stated that Russian vessels towing the ship home was the safest solution for Finland. Hours after the incident, Finland reported a Russian helicopter violation of its airspace, while Poland stated that two Russian missiles landed on its territory on Friday near ongoing European military exercises.

Ukrainian officials condemned the latest escalation, with human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets describing the attacks as part of a genocidal campaign. The widespread bombardment underscores the persistent danger to civilians as the conflict approaches its five-year mark, continuing to strain emergency response infrastructure across multiple regions.

stories.title: چینی محققین نے موروثی گنج پن کے علاج کے لیے برقی کنگھی تیار کر لی
stories.summary:
بیہانگ یونیورسٹی اور دیگر چینی اداروں کے محققین نے ایک ایسی ’برقی کنگھی‘ تیار کی ہے جو موروثی گنج پن کے علاج میں مدد دے سکتی ہے۔ اس تحقیق کے نتائج تین نومبر کو سائنسی جریدے نیچر کمیونیکیشنز میں شائع ہوئے۔ اس کنگھی کا نام ’ڈی ٹینگل‘ رکھا گیا ہے، جو سنہ 2010 کی فلم ٹینگلڈ سے متاثر ہے۔

موروثی گنج پن کو اینڈروجینیٹک ایلوپیشیا کہا جاتا ہے جو دنیا بھر میں ڈیڑھ سے دو ارب افراد کو متاثر کرتا ہے۔ اس کیفیت میں بالوں کی جڑیں کمزور ہو کر سکڑتی جاتی ہیں۔ موجودہ علاجوں میں دوائیوں کا پورے جسم پر اثر انداز ہونا یا جلد اور جڑوں کو نقصان پہنچنے کا خطرہ ہوتا ہے۔

اس نئی کنگھی کے دندانوں میں الیکٹروڈز نصب ہیں جو سر کی جلد میں برقی میدان پیدا کرتے ہیں۔ یہ برقی میدان خلیات کی بیرونی تہہ میں عارضی تبدیلی لاکر بالوں کی نشوونما کے لیے استعمال ہونے والے مادوں کو تقریباً 660 مائیکرومیٹر گہرائی تک پہنچاتا ہے، جبکہ روایتی طریقوں میں یہ گہرائی 74 مائیکرومیٹر ہوتی ہے۔

محققین کے مطابق چوہوں پر کیے گئے تجربات میں ایک ماہ کے اندر بال تقریباً پورے اس حصے میں دوبارہ اگ آئے جہاں پہلے بال موجود نہیں تھے۔ تاہم ماہرینِ امراضِ جلد پروفیسر راڈ سنکلیئر اور ڈاکٹر رامون گریمالٹ نے خبردار کیا ہے کہ یہ نتائج صرف چوہوں پر حاصل ہوئے ہیں اور چوہوں کی جلد انسانوں سے مختلف ہونے کی وجہ سے انسانی نتائج کے لیے مزید طبی تجربات کی ضرورت ہے۔

stories.title: رحیم یار خان میں گاڑی نہر میں گرانے کا ڈرامہ قتل کے مقدمے میں بدل گیا
stories.summary:
پنجاب کے ضلع رحیم یار خان میں 7 اکتوبر کی صبح واہی جمن شاہ کے قریب ایک کار نہر میں گرنے کی اطلاع ملی۔ ریسکیو 1122 کے غوطہ خوروں نے گاڑی اور مبینہ سوار کی تلاش شروع کی۔ آپریشن کے دوران غوطہ خور رئیس عرفان ساجد پانی میں پھنس کر جاں بحق ہو گئے، جبکہ گاڑی سے کوئی سوار نہیں ملا۔

تھانہ کوٹ سمابہ میں لاپتہ شخص کی والدہ کی مدعیت میں اغوا کا مقدمہ درج کیا گیا، جن کا کہنا تھا کہ ان کا بیٹا کاروباری لین دین کے تنازع اور چیک پر زبردستی دستخط کروانے کی وجہ سے پریشان تھا۔ تاہم پولیس کو لاپتہ شخص کی ایک ویڈیو بھی ملی جس میں وہ خود کو مشکلات کا شکار بتا کر خودکشی کا ارادہ ظاہر کر رہا تھا۔

17 اور 18 نومبر کی درمیانی شب پولیس نے مبینہ طور پر لاپتہ ہونے والے شخص کو اس کے گھر سے گرفتار کر لیا۔ تحقیقات سے معلوم ہوا کہ ملزم نے قرض خواہ افراد سے بچنے کے لیے خود ساختہ واقعہ ترتیب دے کر گاڑی نہر میں گرائی اور روپوش ہو گیا۔

اس خود ساختہ واقعے کی وجہ سے ہونے والے ریسکیو آپریشن میں ریسکیو اہلکار عرفان ساجد کی موت واقع ہوئی، جس پر پولیس نے ملزم کے خلاف تعزیراتِ پاکستان کی دفعہ 302 کے تحت مقدمہ درج کر لیا۔ ملزم کو عدالت میں پیش کر کے جسمانی ریمانڈ حاصل کیا گیا جبکہ ملزم کی والدہ اور بھائی نے گرفتاری کو ناانصافی قرار دیتے ہوئے قانونی دفاع کی تیاری شروع کر دی ہے۔

stories.title: Why Pakistan's Most Profitable Firms Choose Dividends Over Investment
stories.summary:
Low investment levels in Pakistan are frequently attributed to limited access to finance and high borrowing costs, prompting governments to court foreign capital and promote savings instruments. Between 2005 and 2025, total investment averaged just 15.7% of GDP, significantly lower than the 29.8% average for lower-middle-income countries, while private investment hovered near 10% of GDP. Successive administrations have pursued foreign direct investment through incentives and high-profile visits, yet FDI has averaged under one per cent of GDP, among the lowest globally.

However, data from the State Bank of Pakistan suggests that a shortage of funds is not the primary barrier for major corporations. Between 2005 and 2025, non-financial corporations listed on the stock market earned Rs20.7 trillion after tax in today's prices and distributed Rs10.7 trillion—more than half—as cash dividends. High payout ratios were recorded across 15 of those 21 years, reaching Rs500 billion in fiscal year 2025 alone. Sectors such as food, autos, and chemicals reported dividend distributions between 57% and 63%. Furthermore, the top-performing private firms and multinational subsidiaries distributed 54% and 68% of their profits respectively, indicating that the nation's wealthiest enterprises possess sufficient capital but lack incentives to reinvest domestically.

According to economic analysis, high dividend payouts reflect a lack of viable long-term investment opportunities due to macroeconomic volatility and institutional weakness. Pakistan has entered its 24th International Monetary Fund programme amid recurring boom-and-bust economic cycles, creating severe uncertainty that discourages capital commitment. Additionally, weak regulatory and judicial enforcement severely undermines contract security, with the World Justice Project's 2025 Rule of Law Index ranking Pakistan 130th out of 143 countries. Complex production and supply chain investments require predictable legal frameworks, which are currently absent.

Recent policy measures have tended to rely on discretionary arrangements rather than institutional reform. The establishment of the Special Investment Facilitation Council in 2023 allows for case-by-case regulatory relaxations, a practice critics warn reduces transparency. Furthermore, constitutional amendments, including the 26th and 27th amendments, have been criticized by bodies such as the International Commission of Jurists for weakening judicial independence and executive accountability, reinforcing the environment of uncertainty that deters domestic reinvestment.

stories.title: Netanyahu and Eisenkot Hold Coalition Talks Amid Structural Policy Disagreements
stories.summary:
Delegations representing caretaker Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud party and opposition rival Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party met at a hotel in Herzliya near Tel Aviv on Sunday to resume negotiations on forming a coalition government. Following inconclusive October elections that left neither political bloc with an absolute majority, Eisenkot holds the mandate to form a government until December 6, with a potential 14-day extension. Eisenkot's 48-member bloc requires 61 lawmakers for a majority and remains divided over whether to pursue an alliance with ultra-Orthodox parties, seek cooperation with Arab factions, or form a national unity government with Likud.

Netanyahu is advocating for a national unity government that could feature a rotational premiership, an arrangement that would simultaneously help protect him from ongoing corruption charges and allow him to oppose an independent commission of inquiry into the security failures preceding the October 7, 2023 Hamas raid. However, Eisenkot built his campaign on refusing to serve in a cabinet led by Netanyahu, a stance reinforced by his ally Naftali Bennett, who reiterated his refusal to join any coalition involving Netanyahu or his bloc.

During Sunday's talks, Likud outlined strict conditions for entering a unity government, demanding an end to personal attacks against outgoing officials and the exclusion of Arab parties from the coalition. Likud also insisted on a unified stance rejecting a Palestinian state, maintaining Israeli military control over territories in Syria, Lebanon, and the Gaza Strip, and reaching a compromise regarding the military conscription of ultra-Orthodox Jews. Arab parties secured a record 19 seats in the legislature but remain opposed to Netanyahu remaining in power, creating deep friction within the prospective coalition alignments.

Eisenkot warned on Friday that he would not permit prolonged negotiations and stood prepared to submit an emergency national government to parliament. While details were limited, this approach could involve forming a minority government backed by core opposition parties before attempting to broaden its base. Right-wing figures within the opposition, such as Avigdor Liberman, reject working with Arab lawmakers and instead advocate for partnering with ultra-Orthodox parties, complicating Eisenkot's path to securing a governing majority.

stories.title: Kuwait Gives 516 Residents 30 Days to Update Their Residential Addresses
stories.summary:
Kuwait’s Public Authority for Civil Information has officially removed the residential address registrations of 516 individuals from its official records. The announcement was published on Sunday, November 22, 2026, in the official gazette, Kuwait Al-Youm. The affected individuals have been given a strict 30-day window to provide updated address information to avoid financial penalties.

According to the authority, these cancellations were initiated following requests and declarations submitted by property owners, while some entries were deleted because the buildings in question had been demolished. PACI has instructed all impacted residents to register their current residential addresses within the stipulated period. This can be done either by visiting PACI offices directly or by using Kuwait’s Sahel government application after preparing the necessary supporting documents.

Failing to comply with the directive within the 30-day deadline will expose individuals to penalties under Article 33 of Law No. 32 of 1982. Under this legislation, violators can face fines reaching up to KD 100 for each concerned person. This measure underscores the significance of maintaining accurate and current civil information within Kuwait's official registry systems, prompting authorities to urge quick verification before the deadline expires.

stories.title: Port Qasim Coal Conveyor Breakdown Disrupts Power Plants and Industries in Pakistan
stories.summary:
The sole coal-handling conveyor system at the Pakistan International Bulk Terminal located at Port Qasim has been non-functional since November 18, severely impacting imported coal supplies. The breakdown occurred during the discharge of coal from the vessel Pegasus 8, which officials attributed to the excessively dusty nature of Tanzanian coal combined with sharp pieces of foreign iron mixed into the cargo. Consequently, coal discharge rates dropped dramatically from the usual 30,000 tonnes down to 3,000 tonnes per day.

This disruption has caused major operational hurdles for public and private power plants, as well as cement and textile industries, at a time when the broader power sector is already grappling with reduced hydroelectric availability and liquefied natural gas supply disruptions. With vessels facing extended waiting times, terminal congestion has worsened. The state-run Jamshoro Power Company warned that incoming shipments are heavily delayed, putting critical fuel stocks and electricity generation for the national grid at immediate risk.

Jamshoro Power Company noted that incoming shipments and upcoming vessels could accumulate between $2 million and $3 million in demurrage charges, alongside potential monthly capacity payment losses of approximately Rs2.2 billion due to insufficient coal inventory. Although JPC formally requested PIBT to declare force majeure to help mitigate financial and insurance losses, PIBT rejected the request on the grounds that discharging operations are still ongoing conventionally at a slower pace. Repairs are estimated to take eight to 10 days.

stories.title: Journalist Mehdi Hasan Discusses Silicon Valley Gatekeeping and Media Independence at Doha Festival
stories.summary:
British-American journalist Mehdi Hasan addressed the evolving media landscape during a talk titled 'The New Gatekeepers' at the Doha Film Festival on November 22, 2026. Reflecting on his career across major networks like the BBC, CNN, Al Jazeera, Sky News, and MSNBC, alongside his independent venture Zeteo, Hasan discussed how the internet and social media have democratized information access. He noted that anyone with a microphone, camera, and Wi-Fi connection can now potentially reach mass audiences, shifting information control away from traditional gatekeepers.

However, Hasan pointed out that this transformation has effectively outsourced news gatekeeping to Silicon Valley. Technology executives such as Elon Musk and Mark Zuckerberg now wield immense influence over platforms like WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook, and Threads, where a vast portion of the global population accesses news. He cautioned that algorithmic control can severely damage traditional publishers and warned that independent media outlets are not entirely free from outside pressures, facing unique challenges such as 'audience capture' when funded directly by subscribers.

Addressing the broader crisis of trust, Hasan argued that journalism itself is not fundamentally flawed, but rather that institutions, individuals, and specific practices have lost public confidence. He maintained that corporate media remains indispensable because independent outlets often lack the resources and expertise required for large-scale foreign coverage and deep investigative reporting. Furthermore, Hasan stated that journalists are permitted to hold personal opinions as long as their work remains grounded in facts, drawing a clear distinction between professional objectivity and forced neutrality.

stories.title: Pakistan A Captain Abdul Samad Praises Team Effort Following Asia Cup Win Over India
stories.summary:
Pakistan A captain Abdul Samad credited both his batters and bowlers for a comprehensive 48-run victory over India in the Asia Cup Rising Stars tournament. Speaking after the match, Samad highlighted the aggressive opening partnership between Shamyl Hussain and Maaz, noting that their early performance put heavy pressure on the opposition. He also commended Hasan Nawaz for delivering an outstanding individual performance during the encounter.

Explaining tactical decisions, Samad mentioned that the dry nature of the pitch influenced his decision to bat first after winning the toss. Recognizing India's strength as a competitor, he emphasized the necessity for Pakistan to post a total exceeding 300 runs on that surface. Pakistan ultimately set a target of 314 runs, which proved successful as the bowling attack systematically contained the opposition.

During India's chase, captain Tilak Varma scored a century off 148 balls, while Abhishek Sharma contributed 70 runs, but their efforts ultimately fell short as India was bowled out 48 runs shy of the target. Several Indian batters failed to score, while Pakistan's bowling attack was led by Ali Raza and Hasan Nawaz, who claimed three wickets each, alongside Muhammad Imran Randhawa, who picked up two wickets.

stories.title: Pakistan Needs Alternative Growth Strategies Amid Global Trade Shifts
stories.summary:
Economic debates in Pakistan often focus on the Real Effective Exchange Rate (REER), which reached 110 in October 2026. While some critics view this as artificial management, experts like Dr Ishrat Husain note that REER has a limited purpose and does not measure balance-of-payments sustainability or exporter competitiveness. Indicators such as a minor current account surplus, a primary fiscal surplus, and rising reserves suggest no immediate crisis, with the rupee’s value driven by robust dollar inflows from exports and remittances alongside positive real interest rates.

Despite macroeconomic stability, Pakistan's sustainable growth rate remains limited to around 4 percent annually, split between 2.5 percent population growth and actual productivity. Experts frequently advocate for enforced currency devaluation and import liberalisation to foster export-led growth. However, political economy constraints mean governments often prioritize specific societal segments and short-term stabilisation over sweeping economic overhauls, failing to fully implement these export strategies.

Furthermore, global trade dynamics pose a severe challenge to traditional export-led industrialisation. Following decades of protectionism and structural adjustment, Pakistan has achieved limited integration into global value chains, primarily restricted to textiles. With advancements in artificial intelligence and robotics lowering global labor costs, and major economies favoring on-shoring, protectionism, and regional trade blocs anchored around China, Pakistan's cheap and unskilled labor may struggle to find a viable role in international markets.

This evolving multipolar world order raises critical questions about whether the global environment still permits export-led growth for developing nations. As geopolitical fracturing and tariffs complicate foreign direct investment, economists suggest that Pakistan must explore alternative domestic economic strategies. Without a backup plan to combine labor and capital productively, the country risks remaining trapped in an anaemic growth baseline with limited prospects for poverty reduction and employment generation.

stories.title: نایاب بیماری کا شکار چھ سالہ عائزہ جو بڑی ہو کر ڈاکٹر بننا چاہتی ہیں
stories.summary:
انڈیا کی ریاست کیرالہ کے ایک گاؤں کی چھ سالہ بچی عائزہ، جنہیں پیار سے ’ٹھکو‘ کہا جاتا ہے، ’کیوٹِس لیکسا‘ نامی نایاب جینیاتی بیماری کا شکار ہیں۔ اس بیماری کی وجہ سے ان کی جلد اپنی لچک کھو چکی ہے اور وہ کسی 80 سالہ بزرگ جیسی دکھائی دیتی ہیں۔

کیوٹِس لیکسا جلد کی ایک نایاب حالت ہے جو دنیا بھر میں تقریباً 400 افراد کو متاثر کرتی ہے۔ اس بیماری کی وجہ سے عائزہ کو اکثر نزلہ، کھانسی اور بخار رہتا ہے اور انہیں مہینے میں کئی دن ہسپتال میں گزارنے پڑتے ہیں۔ ڈھائی سال کی عمر میں ان کی ہرنیا اور آنکھ کی دو سرجری بھی ہو چکی ہیں۔

عائزہ کے والد اکھل نجی کمپنی میں سکیورٹی گارڈ ہیں اور ان کے لیے علاج کے اخراجات پورے کرنا مشکل ہے۔ اس بیماری کا کوئی مکمل علاج موجود نہیں ہے اور اس کا اثر اندرونی اعضا پر بھی پڑ سکتا ہے۔ تاہم ان تمام مشکلات کے باوجود عائزہ پہلی جماعت کی طالبہ ہیں اور بڑی ہو کر ڈاکٹر بننا چاہتی ہیں۔

عائزہ کو رقص، ڈرائنگ اور گانا پسند ہے۔ سنہ 2024 میں ان کا ایک انسٹاگرام اکاؤنٹ بنایا گیا جس پر ان کے 25 ہزار سے زیادہ فالوورز ہیں۔ اگرچہ ماہرینِ نفسیات نے کم عمر میں سوشل میڈیا کے استعمال پر خبردار کیا ہے، لیکن عائزہ کے والدین کا ماننا ہے کہ اس سے دنیا کو ان کے بارے میں مثبت پہلو دیکھنے کو ملے گا۔

stories.title: Mehdi Hasan Discusses Independent Journalism and Silicon Valley Gatekeepers at Doha
stories.summary:
British-American journalist Mehdi Hasan spoke at the Doha Film Festival about the evolving media landscape during a session titled The New Gatekeepers. Drawing on his career with major networks like the BBC, CNN, Al Jazeera, Sky News, and MSNBC, Hasan examined how the rise of social media and digital platforms has altered the dissemination of news. He noted that while information access has been democratized, news gatekeeping power has largely transferred to Silicon Valley executives such as Mark Zuckerberg and Elon Musk.

Discussing his transition to independent journalism through his company Zeteo after his MSNBC show was canceled, Hasan addressed the concept of editorial independence. He acknowledged that independent outlets are not entirely free from pressures, citing 'audience capture,' where creators feel compelled to tell subscribers what they want to hear. He shared that during the 2024 US election, he faced subscriber cancellations from individuals with opposing views, highlighting the difficulties of maintaining a neutral editorial space.

Hasan emphasized that every journalist effectively has to function as a content creator now, though he clarified that not every content creator or YouTuber qualifies as a journalist. He also maintained that traditional corporate media remains essential for large-scale investigations and foreign coverage, resources that independent startups typically lack. Addressing public distrust, he argued that the issue lies with failing institutions and practices rather than journalism itself, while stressing that objectivity and personal opinions can coexist as long as they are rooted in facts.

stories.title: Pop Star Miley Cyrus Marries Drummer Maxx Morando in California
stories.summary:
Grammy-winning pop star Miley Cyrus has married her longtime partner, drummer Maxx Morando, in a private ceremony in California. The 33-year-old singer shared black-and-white photographs of the event on Instagram on Sunday, featuring captions reading 'M + M' and '11.21.26.' Cyrus wore a backless white silk gown, while the 28-year-old groom donned a classic black suit and white shirt for the Saturday ceremony.

The wedding took place in Palm Springs, arriving roughly a month after the couple performed 'Let’s Get Married' together at the Hollywood Bowl. The track is included on Cyrus's latest studio album, Bass Persuades. Representatives for the couple did not immediately respond to requests for comment regarding the nuptials.

Cyrus and Morando have been together for approximately five years, having first met on a blind date in 2021. In December, Cyrus publicly discussed her engagement to the drummer during an appearance on ABC’s Good Morning America. Morando plays drums for Liily, a Los Angeles-based alternative rock band associated with Atlantic Records. Cyrus was previously married to actor Liam Hemsworth, who filed for divorce in Los Angeles in 2019.

stories.title: India Seeks Five Wickets for Victory Against New Zealand in Wellington
stories.summary:
India needs five wickets in the final session to secure victory in the first Test after reducing New Zealand to 206-5 at tea on the final day in Wellington. Playing at the Basin Reserve on Monday, the Black Caps trail India's first-innings total of 720-9 declared by 146 runs, with their primary goal being to bat out the remainder of the day to salvage a draw.

Shortly after lunch, Anshul Kamboj made a breakthrough by dismissing Tom Blundell for 15. Although the delivery initially appeared to miss the bat, an Indian review using DRS technology detected a faint nick, sending Blundell back to the pavilion. Daryl Mitchell and first-innings centurion Glenn Phillips subsequently resumed New Zealand's rearguard effort for the final session of the match.

Earlier in the day, spinner Washington Sundar claimed the opening wicket by removing Devon Conway for 65 via a catch from Rishabh Pant. Rachin Ravindra followed for 37 after hitting a miscued shot off Prasidh Krishna to KL Rahul in the slips. Krishna finished as the pick of the Indian bowlers with figures of 2-22. The second and final Test of the series is scheduled to begin in Christchurch on Friday.

stories.title: Tata Steel to Acquire Major Stake in APL Apollo Tubes
stories.summary:
India’s Tata Steel announced on Monday that it has agreed to acquire a 26.38% stake in APL Apollo Tubes for approximately 155.11 billion rupees, equivalent to $1.67 billion. As part of the transaction, Tata Steel will purchase shares from existing holders at 2,100 rupees per share, marking a 1% discount compared to the stock's closing price on Friday.

In accordance with Indian takeover regulations, Tata Steel will additionally launch an open offer to secure another 26% holding in the company. If the open offer achieves full subscription, Tata Steel's total ownership in APL Apollo will increase to about 52.38%, granting it majority control of the structural steel tube maker.

The acquisition aligns with steelmakers' strategies to boost exposure to higher-margin, value-added downstream segments, helping offset volatility in commodity steel markets. APL Apollo, India's largest structural steel tube manufacturer, has experienced strong demand driven by construction, infrastructure, and industrial projects. The company's stock has risen nearly 11% over the year, contrasting with a 1.2% decline for Tata Steel.

stories.title: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Commits to Annual Federal Contributions Under Governor’s Rule
stories.summary:
During the first 43 days of emergency and governor's rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, the interim administration signed a memorandum of understanding committing the province to an annual cash grant of Rs157 billion to the federal government. This amount forms part of Rs1.035 trillion sought from all four provinces for national economic initiatives. Previously, the ousted PTI government and dysfunctional chief minister Sohail Afridi had withheld this contribution.

The agreement formally covers Rs17.7 billion already deducted at source from KP's National Finance Commission share between July and October 2026. Meanwhile, uncertainty surrounds Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's announced Rs160 billion package for the province from October 22, including whether it represents fresh funding or includes existing allocations for newly merged districts, and how funds will be distributed.

Under recent notifications, administrative authority has been split. Twelve districts are placed under an additional chief secretary acting as administrator for the Area Development Secretariat, while the remaining 24 districts fall under Governor Faisal Kareem Kundi and an 11-member advisory council. The KP Finance Department retains financial authority and budgetary control in consultation with the secretariat.

Political figures and former officials have raised questions regarding the new arrangement. Former finance adviser Muzzammil Aslam noted that provincial financial management requires adjustment, while former minister Taimur Jhagra argued the separate secretariat in Peshawar makes little difference. Former secretary Dr Akhtar Ali Shah questioned how a parallel structure would improve security when direct federal control previously failed in tribal areas.

Information adviser Samar Haroon Bilour defended the new administrative division, stating that 70 percent of resources will go to the 12 ADS districts and 30 percent to the other 24. She credited Prime Minister Shehbaz with implementing the secretariat concept, which brings the province's ongoing financial arrangements and reliance on federal transfers into sharper focus.

stories.title: Pakistan Information Commission Directs PTV to Disclose Foreign Trip Expenses
stories.summary:
The Pakistan Information Commission has ordered the Pakistan Television Corporation to disclose complete details of foreign trips undertaken by its officials at public expense starting from January 2025. Signed by Information Commissioner Ijaz Hassan Awan and Chief Information Commissioner Shoaib Ahmad Siddiqui, the directive instructs PTV's managing director to provide the information within 10 days and submit a copy to the commission.

The ruling came in response to an appeal filed on June 21, 2026, by journalist and Right to Information activist Saddia Mazhar. She had requested the names of officials who travelled abroad, team compositions, the nature of their assignments, and expenditures incurred by the government or PTV for events and coverage from January 2025 onward.

PTV resisted the request, arguing in an August 25 written response that the records involved official deployments, security considerations, and operational sensitivities. The state broadcaster invoked exemptions under Section 16(d)(ii) and (iii) of the Right of Access to Information Act, 2017, maintaining that the tours covered high-level government engagements and prime ministerial visits.

The commission rejected PTV's position, stating that the requested data relates to the utilization of public funds from a public body's allocated budget and falls under sections 5(g) and 6(b) of the same act. The commission concluded that information about public expenditure constitutes public information subject to disclosure.

Furthermore, the commission dismissed PTV's claims regarding commercial interests and financial damage, noting that the broadcaster failed to establish how releasing the details would harm its operations. It ruled that describing information as confidential or sensitive without proving legal exemptions does not justify withholding public records.

stories.title: Indian Rupee Set for Further Gains Driven by Foreign Equity Inflows
stories.summary:
The Indian rupee is expected to extend its appreciation, supported by sustained foreign buying in domestic equities as a deepening technology rout and easing US rate hike expectations alter market dynamics. Currency traders anticipate the rupee to open within the 92.60 to 92.64 range against the dollar, following a Friday close of 92.67.

Last week, the currency advanced in every trading session, with the momentum accelerating sharply on Friday. Heavy dollar sales by foreign banks acting for custodial clients pushed the exchange rate past the 93-per-dollar threshold. This recovery marks a significant turnaround from previous weeks when the currency risked sliding toward 97 per dollar, aided by central bank interventions and measures restricting dollar demand.

A rotation away from artificial intelligence-heavy markets is currently driving fresh capital into Indian equities. Following a sharp Friday selloff that saw the Nasdaq Composite drop over five percent, overseas investors poured more than $1 billion into Indian stocks on that day alone, bringing total monthly inflows to $12.9 billion.

A private sector bank currency trader noted that the heavy inflows are pushing the rupee to unexpected levels, describing the rally as overstretched and the currency as overbought. Nonetheless, price action continues to command market compliance despite apparent sustainability concerns.

Additional support for the rupee on Monday stems from scaled-back expectations for a Federal Reserve rate hike in December amid heightened risk aversion. Although a 25-basis-point increase remains the primary expectation, it is no longer fully priced in, leaving a small probability that rates may remain unchanged.

stories.title: Australian Shares Projected to Open Lower Amid Weak Commodity Prices
stories.summary:
Australian shares are poised to open on a negative note, with mining stocks expected to face downward pressure from declining copper and gold prices. Overall market sentiment remains fragile following soft employment data from the previous week, which heightened concerns regarding an impending economic slowdown.

Local share price index futures declined by 0.6 percent, representing a 36.6-point discount relative to the underlying S&P/ASX 200 index close. The benchmark index itself had previously dropped 1.6 percent during Friday's trading session.

In neighboring New Zealand, market performance reflected similar regional weakness as the benchmark S&P/NZX 50 index fell by 1 percent during early trading hours. The combined market movements highlight cautious investor sentiment across Australasian financial exchanges.

stories.title: Trump Hosts Meme Coin Gala as Token Value Plummets
stories.summary:
US President Donald Trump is set to headline his third meme coin gala on Sunday night at the Trump National club in Sterling, Virginia. The event targets top holders of the tokens, which have dropped in value from about $75 each to less than $1. Less than 20 months after the initial gala drew 220 wealthy crypto holders, interest has notably declined for the latest gathering.

Organizers noted that 185 crypto wallets qualified for the dinner, though the official website leaderboard listed only 130 wallets at the conclusion of the contest on November 16. These listed wallets held a total of $8.6 million, a sharp decrease from the $148 million recorded for the first dinner in May 2025. The top 29 winners, based on time-weighted holdings between September 30 and November 16, will attend a VIP reception with the president and receive gift bags, while the top four will also obtain an 18-karat gold Trump-branded watch.

An analysis of blockchain data by the nonprofit Public Citizen revealed that more than half of the publicly listed wallets for Sunday's dinner are connected to crypto exchanges that prohibit US-based users, suggesting foreign ownership. Meanwhile, Democratic leaders in the House and Senate have pledged to investigate potential conflicts of interest regarding the Trump family's business dealings and plan to propose legislation banning such activities. The White House and the Trump Meme Coin project did not respond to requests for comment, though the administration has previously defended the president's business interests.

Financial disclosures indicate that the Trump meme coin has generated at least $635 million for the Trump family. In total, the Trumps earned at least $2.3 billion through April from their four primary crypto ventures, alongside a stake in the Trump Media & Technology Group valued at approximately $430 million. However, outside investors across five main crypto-linked projects have collectively lost over $5 billion as asset values have dropped to record lows.

stories.title: US Futures Recover While Asian Markets React to Tech Selloff
stories.summary:
US stock futures advanced on Monday as authorities in Asia worked to stabilize sliding stock markets following a severe market wipeout for technology and chip stocks linked to the artificial intelligence boom. Investors have grown increasingly skeptical about whether heavy spending on data centers funded by borrowed money will yield returns quickly enough to justify current high valuations.

Last week, the Nasdaq suffered a 10% drop, marking its largest weekly decline since March 2020, while Taiwan experienced its biggest benchmark fall since 1990. On Monday, Nasdaq 100 futures rebounded by roughly 3% and S&P 500 futures increased by 2% during early trading. Taiwan's stocks steadied, whereas South Korean shares dropped about 4% to a 10-month low before finding support. South Korea's finance minister planned a press conference regarding a potential market stabilization fund to help mitigate further declines.

Market strategists noted that US markets spent three sessions in panic territory last week, raising questions about whether sufficient momentum exists for a durable market recovery without central bank intervention. Japanese markets remained closed for a holiday, while equities in Hong Kong and China fell to new multi-month lows. Rising interest rates have placed sustained pressure on the wider AI trade spanning power generators, cable makers, and switch manufacturers.

Tensions were further exacerbated by the departure of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and the disappointing debut of AI company Anthropic, which closed 8.5% lower on its first full day of trading. In response to the volatility, Taiwan's financial regulator tightened short-selling rules on Saturday, and Chinese stock exchanges announced support measures including relaxed margin financing requirements.

stories.title: Alice Huang Maintained Chinese Spy Agency Contact During Nvidia Affair
stories.summary:
Alice Huang maintained communication with an official from China's Ministry of State Security for over a year during her affair with former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, according to a New York Times report published on Sunday. Citing individuals familiar with intelligence reports, the publication stated the contact occurred from the spring of 2025 through the fall of this year. Representatives for Jensen Huang declined to comment, while Nvidia and the Chinese embassy in Washington did not immediately respond.

The revelations arrive as US officials maintain caution regarding initial suggestions that Alice Huang acted as a spy, following an October 29 article that prompted Jensen Huang's resignation two weeks later and a steep drop in Nvidia's stock price. US Attorney General Todd Blanche and US Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton both stated that investigations into Huang and her company remain ongoing, with no official conclusion reached regarding espionage.

Alice Huang previously led Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based customer responsible for billions in Nvidia chip sales. US authorities have investigated Megaspeed since 2024 over allegations that it smuggled advanced AI semiconductors to China. The unfolding scandal has intensified bipartisan scrutiny in Washington concerning export controls, with lawmakers questioning whether the Trump administration has been insufficiently strict in regulating the high-end technology.

stories.title: Mehdi Hasan Examines Silicon Valley Gatekeeping and Independent Media Pressures
stories.summary:
Journalism has experienced a profound shift due to social media and independent platforms, bringing both democratized access and new challenges. Speaking at the Doha Film Festival during a talk titled 'The New Gatekeepers,' British-American journalist Mehdi Hasan discussed the evolving media ecosystem and his transition to independent journalism through his company, Zeteo, following the cancellation of his MSNBC show.

Hasan noted that historical news gatekeeping restricted mass communication to billionaires, corporations, and governments who controlled technology. While modern digital tools allow anyone with a microphone and internet connection to reach broad audiences, Hasan emphasized that journalism still requires professional standards and fact-checking. However, he argued that power has largely shifted to Silicon Valley executives like Elon Musk and Mark Zuckerberg, whose algorithms and platforms influence the news consumption of billions, sometimes destabilizing publishers.

Addressing the independence of alternative media, Hasan stated that independent outlets are not as independent as they could be. Although they often rely on subscribers rather than corporate or government funding, they face the pressure of 'audience capture,' where outlets risk tailoring their content to satisfy paying subscribers. He shared that Zeteo experienced subscription cancellations during the 2024 US election from audiences with opposing viewpoints, highlighting the difficulty of preserving an objective editorial space.

Furthermore, Hasan observed that journalists must increasingly act as content creators, a dual role he described as a double-edged sword. He argued that institutional failures have eroded public trust rather than an inherent flaw in journalism itself, noting that traditional media remains vital because independent organizations often lack the resources for large-scale foreign coverage and deep investigative reporting.

stories.title: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif to Visit Russia and Iran
stories.summary:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif is scheduled to embark on his first official three-day visit to Russia starting November 30. During this trip, he plans to meet with Russian President Vladimir Putin to discuss bilateral ties, energy cooperation, defense, trade, regional security, and investment agreements. Key topics are expected to feature the revival of Pakistan Steel Mills, which was originally established with Russian assistance, alongside potential Russian investment in Pakistan's oil and gas sectors and broader industrial development initiatives.

Following his engagements in Russia, Prime Minister Shehbaz will travel to Iran to represent Pakistan at the 18th Economic Cooperation Organisation (ECO) Summit, which takes place on December 3 and 4. Leaders from 10 member states are set to gather in Tehran to deliberate on regional trade, connectivity, energy, transportation, investment, and industrial cooperation.

The upcoming summit in Tehran holds additional significance as it precedes Pakistan assuming the official ECO chairmanship for the 2026-27 term. This diplomatic tour highlights Islamabad's active regional engagement strategy, balancing critical energy and economic discussions in Moscow with multilateral cooperation goals at the ECO forum.

stories.title: US Dollar Eases from Multi-Month Highs Amid Recovering Market Sentiment
stories.summary:
The US dollar retreated from a peak not seen in over a year and a half during early Asian trading on Monday. This downward shift followed a recovery in investor confidence after a market selloff the previous week, accompanied by traders scaling back expectations for aggressive interest rate hikes by the Federal Reserve at its upcoming policy meeting.

Despite the pullback, currency markets saw mixed movements across major pairs. The euro ticked up by 0.1 percent to reach $1.0974, while the Australian dollar gained 0.2 percent to hit $0.6629. Meanwhile, the British pound remained flat at $1.3091 and the New Zealand dollar held steady at $0.5474. The US dollar advanced 0.2 percent against the Japanese yen to trade at 158.63 yen as safe-haven demand for the currency subsided. The overall US dollar index remained flat at 103.80, pulling back from its strongest levels since April 2025.

Expectations for monetary policy have shifted away from drastic measures to control inflation. Data from the CME Group’s FedWatch tool indicates that fed funds futures are currently pricing an 88.6 percent probability of a modest 25-basis-point rate hike during the central bank's December 8-9 meeting. Conversely, the likelihood of a larger 50-basis-point increase, which was discussed a week prior, has been completely removed from market pricing.

In broader financial sectors, cryptocurrencies also experienced subdued activity following a sharp drop on Friday. Bitcoin edged down by 0.1 percent to trade at $60,795.03, while ether recorded a slight decline of 0.2 percent to sit at $1,714.96.

stories.title: Indian Shares Projected to Open Higher Driven by Foreign Inflows
stories.summary:
Indian equities are anticipated to open in positive territory on Monday, positioning the market to extend a four-week winning streak. This upward momentum is primarily supported by ongoing foreign investor inflows into Asia’s third-largest economy, alongside declining oil prices and a broader global rotation away from artificial intelligence-linked stocks.

Market indicators pointed to a favorable start, with GIFT Nifty futures trading at 25,912 points ahead of the opening bell. This follows a strong session on Friday where the benchmark Nifty 50 index closed at 25,800.6 and foreign investors executed net purchases of Indian shares totaling 103.08 billion rupees, equivalent to $1.11 billion. Throughout November, foreign investors have poured a record $13 billion into the market, successfully reducing total year-to-date outflows to $18.4 billion.

This robust performance contrasts with broader regional trends across Asia, where MSCI’s broadest index for Asia Pacific stocks outside Japan declined by 1 percent and South Korean equities fell by 3 percent. These regional losses stemmed from growing investor skepticism regarding massive, debt-fueled expenditures directed toward data centers for artificial intelligence models. India’s Nifty 50 has surged nearly 12 percent over the month, outperforming the regional index, bolstered by upgrades to an "outperform" rating by global brokerages HSBC and Goldman Sachs.

Meanwhile, commodity markets saw Brent crude futures decrease by 0.2 percent to $92.3 per barrel. The contract has experienced a 21.6 percent drop over the course of the month, driven by market expectations of easing geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and a subsequent recovery in regional oil supplies.

stories.title: Global Food Import Bill Expected to Rise 1.9 Percent in 2026
stories.summary:
Total global expenditure on food imports is projected to experience a moderate increase in 2026, reaching $2,267 billion, according to a recent report from the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO). This anticipated figure marks a 1.9 percent rise from the revised 2025 total of $2,224.8 billion, driven primarily by higher import bills for animal products, oil seed complexes, and cereals.

The FAO's Food Outlook highlights that prospects for late 2026 and 2027 remain vulnerable to several variables, including rising food commodity prices, elevated energy costs, adverse weather patterns, and financial difficulties experienced by importing nations. Increased energy expenses have driven up freight rates, while potential supply disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz threaten to restrict fertilizer availability and affect crop yields for 2027. Additionally, the establishment and strengthening of the El Nino phenomenon introduce further regional uncertainties regarding agricultural production.

Income distribution among importing nations regarding this financial rise is shifting significantly compared to previous years. While high-income countries historically accounted for the majority of import bill surges—representing 79 percent of the increase in 2025—their share for 2026 is projected at only 13 percent. Instead, upper-middle-income countries (UMICs) are expected to account for roughly two-thirds of the overall increase, driven largely by resumed cereal purchases and strong demand for oil seeds.

To mitigate potential crises, the FAO has advocated for timely financial assistance and expanded funding options for food and fertilizer imports. The agency warned that persistent commodity price inflation and delayed support could severely increase economic pressure on vulnerable, low- and middle-income importing countries heading into 2027.

stories.title: Global Oil Prices Drop Amid Wider Market Selloff and AI Concerns
stories.summary:
Crude oil prices declined on Monday, extending a three-week losing streak driven by a broader financial market selloff. Investors reacted to anxieties surrounding the capacity of the artificial intelligence sector to stimulate economic growth, causing Asian equities to open lower. In regional trading, South Korea's tech-heavy market fell by 4 percent, alongside declines in China, Hong Kong, and Australia. US equity markets also experienced recent slumps, with the Nasdaq plunging 10 percent the previous week.

Despite the downward pressure in global financial markets, ongoing conflicts linked to the unresolved US-Israeli war against Iran helped limit losses. On Sunday, the Houthi movement asserted it had targeted a Saudi Arabian oil refinery, while multiple incidents involving shipping in the Gulf and near the Strait of Hormuz were reported over the weekend. Mukesh Sahdev, chief oil analyst at Sydney-based XAnalysts, noted that empty ballast vessels are accumulating in crude markets while laden vessels lag behind, indicating that shipping risks will soon impact pricing.

In commodities trading, Brent crude futures decreased by 28 cents, or 0.30 percent, to $92.29 a barrel by 0216 GMT. Meanwhile, US West Texas Intermediate futures dropped 15 cents, or 0.18 percent, to $83.26 a barrel. These movements follow last week's declines of 4 percent for Brent and 5 percent for WTI.

Concurrently, discussions at the COP31 global climate summit in Turkiye collapsed on Sunday for the first time since 2009. Participating nations failed to reach a consensus on integrating a statement regarding the phase-out of fossil fuels into the final text. Major oil-producing nations, including Saudi Arabia, lobbied successfully to omit fossil fuel references, arguing that these resources will remain economically essential for the foreseeable future. Looking ahead, OPEC+ ministers are scheduled to meet on November 29 to establish their 2027 output policy.

stories.title: Pakistan Rice Exports Reach 1.35 Million Tonnes Driven by Basmati
stories.summary:
Pakistan experienced a significant surge in its total rice exports, which climbed by 353,000 tonnes to total 1,351,000 tonnes during the first four months of the 2026-27 fiscal year, spanning from July to October. This growth was largely powered by a 62 percent increase in Basmati shipments, overcoming severe maritime disruptions across the Middle East, the Red Sea, and the Strait of Hormuz.

Trade figures for the July-October period show that Basmati exports grew by 116,000 tonnes compared to the same timeframe last year, reaching 301,000 tonnes. Non-Basmati shipments also expanded, growing by 140,000 tonnes year-on-year to hit 1,049,000 tonnes. This expansion occurred despite geopolitical tensions involving Iran, route diversions, escalating ocean freight costs, and high marine insurance premiums.

Market analysts attributed the resilience of the premium grain sector to strong agricultural fundamentals and domestic policy support. Key factors included the extension of the Drawback of Local Taxes and Levies scheme through September, large carryover stocks, expanded cultivation areas, double-cropping in specific regions, higher per-acre yields, and favorable weather conditions resulting in a bumper harvest. In the coarse grain category, Pakistani exporters achieved a 16 percent increase in non-Basmati shipments despite intense price competition from heavily subsidized Indian rice and aggressive offers from Thailand, Vietnam, Cambodia, and Myanmar.

Country-specific data for October 2026 identified the Philippines as the primary buyer, importing 87,478 tonnes. Other top destinations during the month included Tanzania at 43,747 tonnes and Kenya at 33,078 tonnes. Additional buyers comprised the United Arab Emirates with 25,305 tonnes, the European Union with 21,200 tonnes, Central Asia with 16,400 tonnes, China with 11,949 tonnes, and Saudi Arabia with 7,655 tonnes.

stories.title: World Economy Faces Growing Pressures Amid Ongoing Conflict With Iran
stories.summary:
Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan warned that the US-Israel military campaign against Iran is imposing an increasingly severe economic toll worldwide, emphasizing the urgent need for a ceasefire to relieve pressure on global markets. Speaking to Turkish broadcaster TRT Haber, Fidan noted that the protracted conflict and absence of a resolution are pushing toward destructive effects that many countries find increasingly difficult to bear.

Fidan stated that diplomatic initiatives to reopen the Strait of Hormuz remain active despite apparent stagnation, confirming recent discussions with the Qatari prime minister regarding the crisis. He proposed a two-track strategy for resolving regional disputes involving Tehran, suggesting that Iran's nuclear program should be managed within US and United Nations frameworks, while regional issues should be addressed directly by neighboring countries.

In a separate interview with TRT World, Pakistan Peoples Party Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari cautioned that failing to secure a peace deal between the US and Iran could cause the conflict to expand far beyond its current boundaries. He highlighted that Pakistan, China, and Turkiye contributed to brokering the initial ceasefire and continue efforts to maintain negotiations. Bhutto-Zardari added that the conflict is slowing global economic growth and worsening poverty, noting that ordinary Americans are fatigued by prolonged Middle East wars.

Bhutto-Zardari also criticized Israel as a regional spoiler that prefers persistent instability. Discussing broader security implications from conflicts in Ukraine and Iran, he noted nations are increasingly reluctant to rely on a single superpower for protection. Consequently, he welcomed the Makkah Defence Alliance—a security pact between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkiye where an attack on one member is considered an attack on all—and expressed hope that Gulf states will eventually join. Additionally, he warned that modern weaponry left behind by the US in Afghanistan is currently falling into the hands of terrorists and criminal gangs, creating a regional security threat.

stories.title: Pakistan Approves Legislative Overhaul to Strengthen Independent Audit Framework
stories.summary:
The Pakistani government has resolved to overhaul the national audit system after the Prime Minister's Federal Board of Revenue Task Force condemned the existing framework as weak, citing its negative impact on local and foreign investment as well as capital market access. Official documents indicate that legislative amendments will be introduced in parliament to implement these reforms, centered around the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan Amendment Bill, 2026.

The federal cabinet approved the proposed bill following extensive consultations and reviews by three ministerial-level committees. A comparable bill was previously passed by the National Assembly in 2021 before being withdrawn from the Senate in 2022. The task force has also recommended modifying the Audit Oversight Board law to enhance tax collection and align national standards with international requirements.

According to official briefing documents, international bodies previously flagged deficiencies in Pakistan's oversight framework. The International Organisation of Securities Commissions declared Pakistan non-compliant regarding independent audit oversight, and the European Union revoked Pakistan's equivalence status for the same. The report noted that developed and developing nations have transitioned from self-regulation by accountancy bodies to independent oversight, with smaller jurisdictions like Sri Lanka, Mauritius, and Botswana already compliant members of the International Forum of Independent Audit Regulators.

The upcoming legislation aims to eliminate the dominance of private auditors and establish a robust oversight mechanism. Key features of the SECP Amendment Bill, 2026, include strengthening the nominating committee for Audit Oversight Board members by replacing the president of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Pakistan with the FBR chairman, prohibiting board members from having ties to audit firms, and empowering the AOB to conduct risk-based inspections of auditors of Public Interest Companies while directly investigating complaints from regulatory authorities.

stories.title: High Costs and Policy Instability Deter Foreign Investment in Pakistan
stories.summary:
Pakistan has achieved hard-won macroeconomic stability, reflected by State Bank reserves rising from under $3 billion in early 2023 to about $21.5 billion and a multi-year low fiscal deficit. Yet, net foreign direct investment (FDI) fell 34 percent in FY26 to $1.64 billion, representing roughly 0.5 percent of GDP in a nation of 250 million people. Because investors evaluate a ten-year horizon rather than immediate gains, three primary structural obstacles continue to discourage capital inflows.

The first major deterrent is exceptionally high utility costs for industry.
